script.base: NYJ is a short home favorite and should lean on Braelon Allen (58 carries, 298 rush yards over weeks 5-7) against LV's 5.29 YPC defense, leading or tied into the second half at a moderate pace near a 46.5 total. LV, as the dog, keeps a split run game (Jeanty 28/64, Washington 16/75) and Cousins, who is -0.01 EPA vs blitz on 81 dropbacks against a 38% NYJ blitz, lives in short and middle throws to Bowers and Tucker rather than a shootout.
script.flip1: NYJ jumps ahead early, clocks Allen into the 20-carry range, and LV abandons the run so Jeanty's rush line dies while Cousins volume piles onto Bowers/Tucker.
script.flip2: LV hangs or leads and the game flips pass-heavy both ways: Allen's carry count stalls under 80.5 rush, Jeanty can see a positive-script carry bump, and Bowers/Wilson/Cooper overs cash together.

matchup.shell: Sharp coverage pages dated Oct 20 are marked CURRENT, but man/zone and MOFO/MOFC rates are not in this pack excerpt, so shell is unstated. Individual CB assignments and route participation are UNAVAILABLE.
matchup.pressure: NYJ blitzes 38%. Cousins is -0.01 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=81) and +0.16 with no blitz, so pressure should cut deep LV shots and push checkdowns. LV blitzes only 27%; Geno Smith is +0.07 vs blitz (n=65) and +0.11 clean, so LV's lighter pressure does not suppress the NYJ run game.
matchup.bleeds: LV run defense is the soft spot: 5.29 YPC allowed and 27 runs of 10+ in 7 games, plus middle 8.24 YPA (41 att), left 7.44 (91), right 7.79 (90), and 19 passes of 20+ on 239 attempts. NYJ is sturdier on the ground (4.32 YPC, 22 runs of 10+) and best on the left (5.82 YPA, 76 att); they bleed the middle (7.85 YPA, 47 att) more than the right (6.77, 90 att), with 17 passes of 20+ on 232 attempts.
matchup.overlap: Core overlap is Allen's 19-carry L3 role into LV's 5.29 YPC / explosive-run defense. Secondary, not bet: Bowers (28 targets, 253 rec yards, 265 air yards L3) and Tucker (24/241/262) attack NYJ's middle, but the 38% blitz that flattens Cousins is the counterweight.

form: Allen is the NYJ offense: 58/298 rush and 13 targets/56 rec yards L3, with Davis 10/29 and Williams 2/7 not threatening the role. Wilson is 20/174/173 air — about 58 yards a game, under a 67.5 line — while Cooper's 12/218/140 looks explosive and possibly one-game inflated versus a 42.5 line, so neither is used. Jeanty's rush role is small and inefficient (28/64, ~2.3 YPC) but his receiving role is real (20 targets, 147 yards); Washington has been the better LV rusher (16/75). Bowers 28/253/265 and Tucker 24/241/262 are the LV pass game; Tucker's 48.5 line vs ~80 L3 yards is too wide to trust without per-game splits, so he is not a leg. Cousins has 3 carries for 6 yards.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Allen has 58 carries and 298 rush yards over the last three games and LV has allowed 5.29 yards per carry plus 27 runs of 10-plus, so a lead back in a NYJ -2 home script should clear 80.5.
edge_players.must_be_true: He stays the every-down back near 18 carries, NYJ is not trailing by multiple scores early, and he is active with no snap cap once inactives post.
edge_players.kills_it: NYJ falls behind and throws, or Davis/Williams steal series, or a late Allen inactive.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Jeanty has just 28 carries for 64 yards over three games while Washington has taken 16 carries for 75, and NYJ allows 4.32 YPC rather than a get-right run defense, so 50.5 is a high bar for a split-back dog. Script-dependent.
edge_players.must_be_true: Washington stays active and keeps the committee, LV does not grab an early lead and grind, and Jeanty stays around 9-12 carries even if his 2.3 YPC mean-reverts some.
edge_players.kills_it: LV leads and features Jeanty for 14-plus carries at even average efficiency, Washington is inactive, or one 15-20 yard run NYJ has been allowing about three times a game.

market_rung_price: Main lines only, no alt rungs in the pack. Braelon Allen rush yards over 80.5 -114 (not rush+rec 100.5 -113.5). Ashton Jeanty rush yards under 50.5 -115. No short-priced alts.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because NYJ spotted LV an early lead, Geno had to throw, and Allen finished in the mid-60s while Isaiah Davis vultured the cheap yards — LV's 5.29 YPC allowed was opponent-quality, not a green light, and stacked boxes held a 19-carry back under 80.5. On the other leg Jeanty's 2.3 YPC was the fluke, not the role: he got 14 carries, Washington was a gadget, NYJ's 4.32 YPC defense was a get-right spot, and one 18-yard run the Jets allow about three times a game pushed him through 50.5. A late inactive on either back, still unpublished, would have voided the read entirely.
slip_story: One story only: favorite controls the ground. NYJ -2 runs Allen into a 5.29 YPC defense while LV's committee dog run game stays broken, so Allen rush over and Jeanty rush under win together. Do not add Bowers/Tucker/Wilson overs or a total under — those need the shootout flip. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player.
